title: Seed2.0 Model Card: Towards Intelligence Frontier for Real-World Complexity
data_curation: Not a focus of this paper. The model card discloses no training-data sources, sizes, filtering or reward design. Its only data discussion is deployment-usage analysis meant to steer development. Opt-in MaaS traffic from the Doubao Collaboration Incentive Program shows that Internet-sector traffic dominates, and that unstructured information processing is the largest single usage scenario, ahead of education and content creation. Agentic-coding trajectories are dominated by frontend work and bug fixing, with Vue.js adopted more than 3x as often as React. It also states that Seed2.0 targets 'systematic ingestion of long-tail domain knowledge'.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. No pretraining, SFT, RL or distillation stages are described. The report says only that optimization is 'shaped by large-scale product feedback': instruction-following robustness, long-tail knowledge and long-context stability are prioritized for Doubao, while code reasoning and front-end generation quality are prioritized for Trae. It also cites 'continued investment in deep reasoning and code-centric training'. The family ships in three sizes (Pro / Lite / Mini) for latency-cost trade-offs, priced at $0.47 / $0.09 / $0.03 per 1M input tokens and $2.37 / $0.53 / $0.31 per 1M output tokens.
method: Not a focus of this paper. Model architecture and training algorithms are not disclosed. Instead, the report contributes an evaluation framework over four advanced dimensions (Scientific Discovery, Vibe Coding, Context Learning, Real-World Tasks) built from Seed-designed benchmarks: LPFQA, Encyclo-K, HLE-Verified, NL2Repo-Bench, AInstein Bench, BABE, DeR2, GDPVal-Verified, XpertBench and WorldTravel. Agentic evals were refactored into pre-built images with flaky cases filtered out. Inference-time pipelines are described: a solve-verify-refine loop for IMO/CMO proofs, an agentic multi-turn Lean+Python setup for Putnam, a VideoCut tool that replays video segments at higher FPS, and 'Thinking with Tracking' prompting (per-frame bounding boxes) for motion tasks.
eval_metrics: Covers 50 image and 24 video benchmarks plus language (AIME, HMMT, IMOAnswerBench, Codeforces Elo, LiveCodeBench v6, GPQA, ARC-AGI, MMLU-Pro, SuperGPQA, MultiChallenge, Frames, MRCR), agentic (SWE-Bench Verified/Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.0, BrowseComp, HLE, τ²-Bench, BFCL-v4, MCP-Mark) and in-house enterprise suites. Baselines are GPT-5.2 High, Claude-Opus/Sonnet-4.5, Gemini-3-Pro and Seed1.8. Seed2.0 Pro headlines: IMO 2025 35/42 and CMO 2025 114/126 (both gold), Codeforces Elo 3020, Putnam-200 35.5% pass@8, ICPC 2025 pass@8 73.02%, MathVision 88.8, VideoMME 89.5, and 75.26% on an in-house Chinese complex-IF benchmark (+2.37 over Seed1.8).
key_results: Seed2.0 Pro reaches gold-medal level on IMO 2025 (35/42) and CMO 2025 (114/126), has a Codeforces Elo of 3020 and scores 73.02% ICPC pass@8 (gold in all five 2025 contests). It reaches 35.5% pass@8 on Putnam-200 (above Seed-1.5-Prover's 26.5), and leads most vision and video benchmarks. The authors admit clear gaps to Claude in coding (SWE-Evo, NL2Repo) and to Gemini on long-tail knowledge (SuperGPQA, SimpleQA-Verified).
evolution_note: Successor to Seed1.5-Thinking/Seed1.6/Seed1.8 and Seed1.5-VL. It marks ByteDance Seed's shift from Olympiad-style reasoning toward agentic, long-horizon real-world tasks and research-level reasoning (Erdős problems, scientific coding). Unlike the Seed1.5-Thinking report, it is a model card with no training recipe. Its contributions are deployment-usage analysis, a ~10x cost advantage over frontier APIs, and a suite of new real-world benchmarks.
